The present invention relates to a method for automatically assisting the landing of an aircraft on a runway, from a return point (A) to a completion point (D) at which the aircraft touches down on the runway, by means of an on-board data-processing device configured to be connected to an altimeter and a deviation meter. The method comprises:

- a return-navigation assistance phase, including:
  - guiding the aircraft from the return point (A) toward the position of the deviation meter (E), on the basis of measurements, transmitted by the deviation meter, of the azimuth deviation of the aircraft relative to a reference direction linking said return point (A) and the position of the deviation meter (E);
  - determining the position of the aircraft at a predetermined capture point (B) aligned with the return point (A) and the position of the deviation meter (E); and
  - guiding the aircraft along a predetermined path from the capture point (B) to a predetermined holding point (C), which is approximately aligned with the axis of the runway, on the basis of altitude data provided by the altimeter and heading and speed data relating to the aircraft; and

- a landing assistance phase, including guiding the aircraft from the holding point (C) to the completion point (D).
outputs.L3:
The invention relates to a method for automatically assisting the landing of an aircraft, implemented by an onboard data-processing device. The method is intended to guide the aircraft from a return point toward a runway touchdown point by using navigation information available onboard the aircraft and measurements supplied by dedicated instruments.

The onboard data-processing device is configured to communicate with at least two measuring instruments: an altimeter and a deviation meter. The altimeter provides altitude measurements of the aircraft, while the deviation meter provides azimuth deviation measurements. These azimuth deviation measurements indicate the angular deviation of the aircraft relative to a reference direction, allowing the onboard device to determine whether the aircraft is properly aligned with a desired guidance direction.

During a return-navigation assistance phase, the aircraft is guided from the return point toward the position of the deviation meter. This guidance is performed by using the azimuth deviation of the aircraft relative to the reference direction. In this way, the aircraft can be progressively directed along a navigation path that leads it toward the area from which the landing approach can be initiated.

As part of the method, the onboard data-processing device determines the position of the aircraft at a predetermined capture point. This capture point is located on an alignment defined by the return point and the position of the deviation meter. The capture point serves as an intermediate reference position from which the aircraft can transition from the return-navigation assistance phase to a more structured approach path leading toward the runway.

Once the aircraft reaches the capture point, it is guided along a predetermined path toward a holding point. The holding point is aligned with the axis of the runway, thereby positioning the aircraft appropriately for the final approach. From this holding point, the method continues with a landing assistance phase, during which the aircraft is guided along the runway axis toward the touchdown point on the runway.

Thus, the invention provides an automated landing-assistance method that uses onboard processing, altitude information, and azimuth deviation measurements to guide an aircraft through successive phases: from a return point to a capture point, from the capture point to a runway-aligned holding point, and finally from the holding point to the runway touchdown point.
outputs.L4:
The invention relates to an onboard data-processing method intended to assist, or automatically control, the landing of an aircraft from a predetermined return point until touchdown on a runway. The method uses data available onboard the aircraft, in particular altitude information supplied by an altimeter and lateral or angular deviation information supplied by a deviation meter, in order to generate guidance instructions that enable the aircraft to follow a defined approach path.

According to the method, when the aircraft reaches or is directed toward a return point, the onboard processing system determines a sequence of navigation objectives leading the aircraft toward the landing runway. These objectives include at least one runway-aligned holding or alignment point positioned so that the aircraft can be brought into a correct approach configuration before final descent. The system processes the measured altitude and deviation data to evaluate the aircraft’s position relative to the desired path and continuously computes corrective commands or guidance indications.

During a first phase, the aircraft is guided from the return point toward the runway-aligned holding point. The deviation meter provides information indicating whether the aircraft is to the left or right of the desired course, or otherwise offset from the intended track, while the altimeter provides the altitude reference needed to maintain or adjust the descent profile. The onboard processor compares these measurements with stored or calculated target values associated with the approach path and determines the necessary heading, attitude, or flight-path corrections.

Once the aircraft reaches the holding or alignment point, the method transitions to a final approach phase. In this phase, the aircraft is guided along a path aligned with the runway axis and descending toward the touchdown zone. The processor continues to use the altimeter and deviation meter data to maintain the aircraft on the proper lateral and vertical trajectory. If deviations are detected, the system generates corresponding corrections so that the aircraft remains aligned with the runway and follows an appropriate glide path.

The method therefore provides continuous assistance from the return point through runway alignment and final descent to touchdown. By defining intermediate points and using onboard sensor inputs to update guidance commands in real time, the invention improves the reliability, precision, and continuity of automated or assisted landing operations. It allows the aircraft to be brought from an initial return position to a stable final approach and then to runway contact with reduced pilot workload and improved landing accuracy.

**The Power of “The”**

“The” is one of the smallest and most common words in the English language, yet it plays an important role in communication. It is called a definite article, and it helps identify a specific person, place, thing, or idea. For example, “a book” could mean any book, but “the book” refers to a particular one that the speaker and listener understand.

Although “the” is short, it gives language clarity and precision. It helps connect sentences to context and makes meaning easier to follow. Without it, English would often sound incomplete or unclear. Phrases like “the sun,” “the world,” and “the future” show how this simple word can point to something unique, familiar, or important.

In writing, “the” may seem ordinary, but it is essential. It guides the reader, shapes meaning, and gives structure to sentences. This tiny word proves that even the simplest parts of language can have great significance.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract for an invention that automatically assists an aircraft landing from a return point A to touchdown point D using an onboard processor connected to an altimeter and deviation meter, with phases through points B and C.
counterfactuals.output: An automatic landing assistance system for an aircraft is disclosed. The system includes an onboard processor operatively connected to an altimeter and a deviation meter and configured to guide the aircraft from a predetermined return point A to a touchdown point D on a runway. The processor determines, from altitude data and lateral or vertical deviation data, successive flight control commands corresponding to a plurality of landing phases extending through intermediate points B and C. During a first phase from point A to point B, the system establishes or captures a return or approach path. During a second phase from point B to point C, the system controls descent and alignment relative to a desired landing trajectory. During a final phase from point C to point D, the system provides flare, glide, and touchdown assistance based on measured altitude and deviation from the intended path. The processor may generate guidance signals for display to a pilot or control signals for an aircraft flight control system, thereby reducing pilot workload and improving landing accuracy and safety.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1
